metadata.summary: Christian Horner says Mercedes and Toto Wolff are finding life in Formula 1 "easier" without the former Red Bull team principal.
metadata.content: Christian Horner says Toto Wolff and Mercedes are finding life 'easier' without him in Formula 1 | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Christian Horner says Toto Wolff and Mercedes are finding life 'easier' without him in Formula 1 Christian Horner discussed his rivalry with Toto Wolff and was quizzed on when he could return to Formula 1 in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports News; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin from Friday evening, live on Sky Sports F1 Tuesday 20 October 2026 15:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains the reasons behind why he left Red Bull Racing Christian Horner says Mercedes and Toto Wolff are finding life in Formula 1 "easier" without the former Red Bull team principal. Horner and Wolff had a huge rivalry over the last decade which culminated in the controversial 2021 season where Max Verstappen ended Mercedes' run of seven successive drivers' titles. Red Bull then became constructors' champions in 2022 as Mercedes began a difficult period, which led to more exchanges between Wolff and Horner before the latter was sacked in July 2025. messages.text: Warner slams 'pathetic' Test crowds in South Africa

metadata.summary: Former batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia.
metadata.content: David Warner slams 'pathetic' crowds for South Africa vs Australia Test matches | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content David Warner slams 'pathetic' crowds for South Africa vs Australia Test matches The first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban was less than a fifth full over the course of the five days; the Kwa-Zulu Natal Cricket Union (KZNCU) have said they will launch a "thorough internal review" into the poorly-attended match at Kingsmead Tuesday 20 October 2026 12:30, UK Image: A cricket supporter sits alone in the stands during the first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban Former batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia. South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban , with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha. "We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa?" former opener Warner said in a social media post on Tuesday. messages.text: Boulter puts rain delays behind her to progress at Japan Open

metadata.summary: A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume.
metadata.content: Japan Open: Katie Boulter puts rain delays behind her as Brit progresses to second round in Osaka | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Japan Open: Katie Boulter puts rain delays behind her as Brit progresses to second round in Osaka Britain's Katie Boulter books place in second round of Japan Open, after defeating home wildcard Himeno Sakatsume; Play had been suspended the day before due to heavy rainfall in Osaka; Watch the Japan Open all this week, live on Sky Sports Tennis Tuesday 20 October 2026 08:41, UK Image: Britain's Katie Boulter progressed to the second round of the Japan Open after victory over Himeno Sakatsume A day after heavy rainfall caused play to be suspended, Britain's Katie Boulter returned to clinch a 6-3 6-1 victory at the Japan Open over wildcard Himeno Sakatsume. The world No 58 concluded a dominant victory in one hour and 32 minutes in Osaka, and she will next face Swiss player Viktorija Golubic for a place in the quarter-finals. The victory gives Boulter a 20-20 record across her last 40 matches, and a confidence boost following a period in which she has only played three matches since September 30, owing to early exits at the China Open (second round) and Wuhan Open (first round). messages.text: England unchanged for World Cup clash vs France with Lewis absent again

metadata.summary: England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: Mikey Lewis absent again as England unchanged for clash vs France despite opening defeat England take on France in Perth on Saturday (7.35am kick-off BST) for second Rugby League World Cup fixture, having been thrashed by Tonga in opener; England play Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on October 30; England Women began their campaign with big win vs Wales in Perth Tuesday 20 October 2026 07:48, UK Image: Mikey Lewis will not feature for England again as England opt for unchanged squad England head coach Brian McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man squad that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga in the tournament opener for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup clash against France. AJ Brimson retains the job at full-back with Jack Welsby again named as an interchange, while Luke Thompson starts at prop in the absence of Morgan Knowles, who suffered an injury in the lead-up to the opening game against Tonga. Veteran centre Kallum Watkins is listed among the reserves as he chases a cap at his fourth World Cup, while there also remains no place in the squad for Mikey Lewis. As per World Cup rules, each side is able to name a six-player bench in each game, but only four of the six players named can be brought on.
